Only methods declared in candy-kv/src, or inherited from a parent declared there, are listed. A type that extends a class outside that tree, such as \RuntimeException, does not show the methods of that class.

Store final class

Main entry point for the candy-kv key/value store.

MethodSummary
__construct(?string $dataDir = null, string $defaultDb = 'default')Create a new Store handle.
set(string $key, string $value, bool $binary = false, ?int $ttlSeconds = null): EntrySet a value.
setWithTtl(string $key, mixed $value, int $ttlSeconds): voidSet a value that automatically expires after $ttlSeconds.
get(string $key, string $fallback = ''): stringGet a value by key.
suggestionFor(string $key): ?stringSuggest the closest existing key to $key, or null when nothing is near enough to help. Backs the CLI's "did you mean" line.
entry(string $key): ?EntryGet the full Entry object for a key (includes metadata).
static sanitizeForTty(string $value): stringRender a stored value safely for a one-line terminal (TTY) listing.
fuzzyFilter(string $query, ?string $dbName = null): arrayFilter entries using fuzzy search on keys.
suggestDatabase(string $dbName): ?stringThe nearest live database name to a typo'd one (kv-048), or null when nothing is close enough. Same codepoint law as the key hint — the two doors must not drift into different edit metrics.
delete(string $key): intDelete one or more keys.
list(?string $pattern = null, ?string $dbName = null, bool $reverse = false, string $mode = 'all', string $delimiter = "\t"): \GeneratorList entries in a database.
setFile(string $key, string $filePath): EntryStore binary data from a file path.
saveTo(string $key, string $filePath): boolWrite binary data from a key to a file path.
listDatabases(): arrayGet the list of all database names.
pruneExpired(): intRemove every already-expired entry from the default database and return how many rows were dropped.
pruneDatabase(string $dbName): intRemove every already-expired entry from one NAMED database (kv-025: pruneExpired() only saw the default db, so expired rows in the other files of the same store were unreachable — prune is a vault-wide hygiene job, not a default-database accident).
isReservedDatabase(string $dbName): boolTrue for the catalogued reserved names (S19). Public so a verb can order its doors honestly: a reserved database EXISTS even though listDatabases() hides it, and the write refusal is the informative answer — not 'does not exist'.
deleteDatabase(string $dbName): boolDelete an entire database (all its entries).
dataDir(): stringGet the data directory path.
defaultDatabase(): stringGet the default database name.
transaction(string $dbName, callable $fn): mixedExecute a callback inside an atomic transaction on a named database.
static splitKey(string $key, string $defaultDb): arrayThe key-spelling law as a pure function: split an import/export key into [database, entry key] using the same rightmost-unescaped-'@' rule Store::set() routes by. Importers derive their per-database transaction roster through HERE, so a key spelled a\@b (a literal at-sign) can never be misread as naming a second database — the naive strrpos() version of this walk used to route {"k@x":5,...} imports through a roster that silently missed x.
static hasRawGlob(string $key): boolkv-043: true when $key carries a * or ? byte that is NOT spelled with the pattern engine's escape. Same single-backslash lookback the '@' split applies — the grammar has no \\ self-escape (kv-007), so "escaped" always means "one backslash immediately before it".
static unescapeGlobKey(string $key): stringkv-043: the pattern engine's unescape as a pure key mapping — drop the backslash that spells a literal */? (\* → *, \? → ?). Every other backslash stays exactly as typed: the grammar has no self-escape, so \<x> for other x is literal text, mirroring Database::globToLike's "a backslash before anything else stays literal" law. This is what makes a get arg spelled ra\*wt name the key ra*wt instead of dying at the pattern gate.
static resolveDataDir(): stringResolve the data directory: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/skate, then $HOME/.config/skate, then the passwd entry's home directory.

SugarCraft\Kv\Import

FlatDocumentNormaliser final class

The normalization law shared by both flat importers (candy-kv-063).

MethodSummary
static validatedOptions(array $options): arrayFail fast on the constructor ttl map (candy-kv-031): the options and a document share one write path, so they must share one law. A raw 'soon' used to leak a TypeError out of resolveTtl's return type where every document-level shape answers with a domain exception.
static ttlMap(mixed $map): arrayThe nested _ttl envelope, shared by the JSON top-level member and the YAML legacy symfony-route line: a map of key → whole seconds, or a refusal naming what arrived instead.
static binaryKeyList(mixed $list): arrayThe _binary name-list envelope: keys whose values are base64 of raw bytes. Without the flag a reimport would store the base64 text as the value, so the list must be exact.
static wholeSeconds(string $subject, mixed $seconds): intWhole seconds or a refusal — is_numeric admits floats and float-shaped strings; the store counts whole seconds, and (int) would silently truncate 1.5 to 1 while the text promises "integer". The subject is the sentence head ('_ttl entry "k"', 'TTL for entry "k"'), so each envelope spelling keeps its own voice on one law.
static resolveTtl(array $ttlMap, string $key): ?int
static validatedEntryKey(string $key, Store $store): voidThe key law pre-writes (candy-kv-030): Store::splitKey is the same authority Store::set routes by, and the walk happens BEFORE any row is committed — under atomic=false the old shape left prefix rows mutated and made the refuse-before-any-write law false for exactly this error class.
static refuseNonScalar(string $key, mixed $value): neverOne non-scalar refusal sentence for both formats (candy-kv-103 wording): the type name is not reliably consonant-led, so the article-free "of type %s" shape carries every get_debug_type value. Declared never because it always throws — the callers' rows-shape law depends on the analyzer knowing the branch cannot fall through.
static commit(Store $store, array $rows, bool $atomic, string $ifExists): ImportReportThe commit step (candy-kv-051 kernel + candy-kv-063 roster).

SizeCap final class

The byte ceilings candy-kv-073 asked for: a multi-hundred-MB document used to buffer itself (and, on the symfony YAML route, several copies of itself) straight into an OOM kill that bypassed every "Import failed:" handler — the kernel, not the CLI, answered the oversized input.

MethodSummary
static refuseOversized(?int $bytes, int $maxBytes, string $source): voidRefuse a known size before touching the bytes.
static readStream($stream, int $maxBytes, string $source): ?stringRead a stream up to the ceiling, refusing the moment it grows past it — an unbounded STDIN never reaches the decoder, let alone the OOM killer. Returns null only on a plain read failure (the caller's door owns that domain message); an over-cap stream throws right here.

Ttl final class

The single documented TTL bound for every write channel.

MethodSummary
static inRange(int $seconds): boolTrue when $seconds is a storable positive TTL inside the horizon.

Version final class

The version string this tool reports on --version.

MethodSummary
static line(): stringThe --version line: plain text, newline-terminated, produced by no state and no host probe — the flag must answer anywhere.
static current(): stringThe version this process reports: the archive stamp when running from a stamped phar, self::CURRENT everywhere else.
static fromPharMetadata(string $path): ?stringThe version a phar archive at $path was built to carry, or null when it names none (unreadable archive, wrong metadata shape, the dev-build sentinel, or an empty stamp). Every refusal is a null, never an exception — --version must answer on a machine whose phar cannot be opened.
static versionFromMetadata(mixed $metadata): ?stringThe judgement on the stamp itself, split out because the archive-open leg is unreachable from a suite that must not build phars: the release namespace strip, the dev-build refusal, and the wrong-type nulls are a pure function over what getMetadata() answers.
static hostArchive(): stringThe filesystem path of the phar this process was launched from, or '' when it was not launched from one — the two-identity law measured on candy-code's real builds and pinned by the bin autoload guard: inside archive-loaded code Phar::running(false) answers the archive path, while the stub context answers '' and there a '.phar'-suffixed __DIR__ is the enclosing archive.
